SOURCE techbetweenthelines.com (Is Apple Down? Live iCloud, iMessage and App Store Status):
Loading the current status.
How this page works
This page shows whether Apple's services are working right now. Every five minutes we read the same feed that powers Apple's System Status page and update what you see above. It covers every service Apple reports on, from iCloud Mail and iMessage to the App Store, Apple Pay and Apple Music.
"Running" means Apple reports no problem. "Issue" means Apple says a service is slow or partly failing. "Outage" means Apple has confirmed the service is down for at least some people. "Maintenance" is planned work.
The same check drives the outage notice you may see at the bottom of other pages on Tech Between the Lines, so the two always agree.
What reader reports mean
Apple's page can lag behind a real problem, and it sometimes never lists a partial one. If something isn't working for you, pick the service above and tap "I'm affected". Once three readers report the same service inside three hours, we show the count here, even if Apple hasn't said anything yet.
Reader reports aren't verified, so treat them as an early sign and not a confirmation. The count for a service resets as soon as Apple marks it as fixed, so every outage starts from zero.
If a service is down for you but shows as running
Check your own connection first, then close and reopen the app or restart the device. If it still fails and other readers are reporting it here, the problem is probably on Apple's side and waiting is the fix. Don't sign out of your Apple Account or reset your settings during an outage. Signing back in can fail until the service returns, which leaves you worse off.
If the problem started right after a software update and Apple's services look fine, it may be a bug and not an outage. Our iOS 27 Bug Tracker lists the problems readers are hitting and what to try.

SOURCE tech.yahoo.com (Apple outage affecting iCloud, Apple Pay and other services ...):
A wide range of Apple services suffered an outage on Tuesday, preventing some users from signing in to iCloud and using services like Apple Pay and Apple Music. The outage appears to be resolved now, with Apple saying it was due to an internal update and not a cyberattack.
According to Downdetector, a site that tracks reports of online service outages, iCloud, Apple Support, Apple Pay, and the App Store all saw spikes in reports Tuesday.
Apple's support page initially indicated issues with iCloud accounts and sign-ins, as well as other services. As of 5:30 a.m. ET Wednesday, Apple's support page showed all services had recovered from the outage.
According to Downdetector, these are the services that saw spikes in outage reports:
- Apple Support
- iCloud,
- Apple Pay
- App Store
- Apple Business Manager
- Apple Music
- Apple Store
- Sign In With Apple
- Apple Card
"Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning," an Apple spokesperson initially told us in a statement Tuesday. "We're working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible."
In addition to iCloud, Apple's support page also flags that AppleCare on Device, which lets you purchase AppleCare on your phone or tablet, experienced an outage. That was alongside Apple Business, Apple School Manager, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps and Schoolwork
Users online reported being signed out of services and unable to sign back in. Others reported being unable to activate new iPhones.
The issues follow a string of outages that have plagued online services over the past week. On Nov. 12, Microsoft Outlook and Teams were knocked out for more than 30 hours due to what Microsoft described as a technical issue. On Nov. 13, a technical issue caused all air traffic across the U.S. to be grounded, leading to thousands of canceled and delayed flights.
On Monday, online services at several major U.S. banks experienced problems for several hours after an issue with JPMorgan Chase's systems. Today, CNN reported that a highly classified communications network used by the National Security Agency (NSA) went down.
